title: How Much Do Legal RAG Systems Still Hallucinate?
abstract: arXiv:2608.14210v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Hallucination is a major challenge for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in the legal domain, where ungrounded answers can lead to serious consequences. To better understand this problem, we conduct a fine-grained analysis of hallucination behavior in eight legal RAG systems across two legal corpora, the GDPR (in English) and a national civil law (in French). Using claim-level and answer-level evaluation, we report on hallucination density and severity, analyze performance across question categories and user personas, and validate our findings on an independent set of 142 legal-expert-authored questions. Our results show that hallucinations remain pervasive, ranging from less than 10% of responses for the best-performing systems to nearly half in the worst case. translated_title: 法律领域的RAG系统仍然会产生多少幻觉？
translated_abstract: 摘要：幻觉是检索增强生成（RAG）系统在法律领域面临的主要挑战，因为无根据的回答可能导致严重后果。为了更好地理解这一问题，我们对八个法律RAG系统在两个法律语料库（英文的GDPR和法语的国内民法）中的幻觉行为进行了细粒度分析。通过基于声明级和回答级的评估，我们报告了幻觉密度和严重程度，分析了不同问题类别和用户画像下的性能，并在一个独立的由142个法律专家撰写的问题集上验证了我们的发现。结果显示，幻觉仍然普遍存在，从表现最佳系统的不到10%的回答到最差情况下的近一半回答。我们进一步发现，包含必须拒绝的错误假设的虚假前提问题，在手工起草的问题上产生了高幻觉率。
tldr: 法律RAG系统即使在最佳情况下仍会产生高达10%的幻觉回答，在最差情况下近一半回答存在幻觉，尤其虚假前提问题显著加剧了幻觉现象。
en_tdlr: Legal RAG systems still hallucinate in up to 10% of responses even in the best cases, and nearly half in the worst, with false-premise questions significantly exacerbating hallucination rates.
